translation_notes: prefixes: DC->dc, DCTERMS->dcterms, OWL->owl, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs

graph.objects(subject, prop) -> m{ {subject} {prop} ?o }, arity 1: both subject and prop are plain Python loop variables (subject from subjects_to_check, prop from the desc_properties priority list), so both interpolate with {expr} rather than being written as terms -- the same treatment INSTRUCTIONS_403 gives a parameter in subject position, extended here to predicate position since prop ranges over a list built from prefixed-name values (dc:description, dcterms:description, rdfs:comment).

graph.subjects(RDF.type, OWL.Ontology) -> m{ ?s rdf:type owl:Ontology }, arity 1 (single named variable ?s): the trav_one_step idiom for g.subjects(p, o), same construction as g.objects(s, p) with subject and object roles swapped.
@graph graph designates the method's own graph parameter as current for the whole body (bound method extracted as a plain function; self is never read), so every m{ } stays bare.

Preserved a real quirk instead of 'fixing' it: the second (global) loop over m{ ?s rdf:type owl:Ontology } is NOT gated on `ontology_iri` being falsy, despite what its own comment says -- it runs unconditionally whenever the first loop returns nothing, including when ontology_iri was given but that subject has none of the three description properties. fixture.ttl's ex:OntoEmpty and driver.py's call_global_fallthrough_quirk exist specifically to prove the translation keeps this behaviour rather than silently correcting it (which INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2 forbids as refactoring).

The true zero-solution case (both loops empty, return None) cannot be reached against the shared fixture.ttl: as soon as any owl:Ontology subject with a description exists anywhere in the file, the unconditional second loop -- see the quirk above -- will always find one, whatever ontology_iri is passed. call_zero_solutions() in driver.py therefore builds its own fresh, unrelated, empty Graph() instead (still fresh per side, as fixture_graph is elsewhere) -- the only way to exercise the empty-result branch without contradicting the quirk test.
ex:NotAnOntology in fixture.ttl carries dc:description but is never typed owl:Ontology and is never passed as ontology_iri: the neighbourhood that must not leak into the global search.
